qa.title: Q1242 (Jun. 13, 2025)
qa.question: What is ability damage?
qa.answer: Ability damage is damage from non-combat sources, including damage from spells and follower abilities. Damage from Strike abilities, although triggered by combat, is considered ability damage.

qa.title: Q1320 (Jun. 13, 2025)
qa.question: I have this follower and a Steelclad Minotaur on my field. If my Steelclad Minotaur attacks a 4-attack enemy follower, how much damage does Steelclad Minotaur take?
qa.answer:
It would take either 2 damage or 1 damage, depending on your decision. When there are multiple abilities modifying damage dealt, the player who controls the follower receiving the damage decides the order the abilities are applied. In this case, depending on the order, the final damage taken can be calculated either of the following 2 ways:

1. Steelclad Minotaur takes 2 damage because you decide to apply Steelclad Minotaur's ability first, reducing the damage to 2. Afterward, this follower's ability would no longer apply.

2. Steelclad Minotaur takes 1 damage because you decide to apply this follower's ability first, replacing 4 damage with 3. Afterward, Steelclad Minotaur's ability would reduce that damage to 1.

qa.title: Q1319 (Jun. 13, 2025)
qa.question: Does this follower's passive ability mean a follower only takes 3 damage per turn?
qa.answer:
No, each instance of damage is treated separately. Example:
- If a follower would take 4 damage twice, it would take 3 damage twice instead.
- If a follower would take 4 damage, then 2 damage, it would take 3 damage instead, then 2 damage as usual.

qa.title: Q1330 (Jun. 13, 2025)
qa.question: My leader's defense is 11 and I have no followers on my field, while my opponent only has a Rabbit Necromancer. I play this follower during my turn and use its Fanfare to destroy Rabbit Necromancer, triggering Rabbit Necromancer's Last Words and bringing my leader's defense to 9. Does this follower's other Fanfare then take effect and give my leader +5 defense?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't. When this follower's Fanfare destroys Rabbit Necromancer, Rabbit Necromancer's Last Words will trigger and becoming pending. When both players control pending abilities, the active player resolves theirs first. In this case, you are the active player, so you would resolve this follower's other Fanfare. At this point, since Rabbit Necromancer's Last Words have yet to take effect, your leader's defense is still 11, so it does not gain +5 defense.

However, if you were to somehow summon this follower during your opponent's turn in this same scenario, Rabbit Necromancer's Last Words would resolve first as your opponent is the active player, so your leader could gain +5 defense from this follower's Fanfare, provided you chose to resolve the select and destroy Fanfare first.
